questions.q: Why are the Israelites to keep the Passover for Yahweh their God in the month of Aviv?
questions.a: The Israelites are to celebrate the Passover each year during the month of Aviv because Yahweh brought Israel out of Egypt in that month.

questions.q: What will the Israelites do to celebrate the Passover?
questions.a: The Israelites will sacrifice some of the flock and the herd in the place that Yahweh will choose.

questions.q: Why are the Israelites to eat no leavened bread or have yeast in all their land for seven days?
questions.a: They are to eat no leavened bread or have yeast during those days to remind them that they came out of the land of Egypt with too much haste for bread to rise.

questions.q: What are the Israelites told about the meat that they sacrifice in the evening on the first day?
questions.a: The Israelites are to make sure there is no meat that they sacrifice in the evening remaining the next morning.

questions.q: Where are the Israelites to offer the sacrifice of the Passover?
questions.a: They are to sacrifice at the place that Yahweh will choose.

questions.q: When will the sacrifice of the Passover be performed?
questions.a: The sacrifice of the Passover is to be performed in the evening when the sun is setting, at the time when the Israelites started to leave Egypt.

questions.q: What are the Israelites supposed to do on the first six days as they celebrate Passover?
questions.a: The Israelites are to eat unleavened bread for six days.

questions.q: What are the Israelites supposed to do on the seventh day as they celebrate Passover?
questions.a: On the seventh day, they are to have a festive assembly and do no work.

questions.q: How do the Israelites determine the start of the Festival of Weeks for Yahweh?
questions.a: The Israelites will count seven weeks from the time they begin to harvest their grain.

questions.q: What contribution do the Israelites give on the Festival of Weeks?
questions.a: They must give Yahweh a freewill offering according to how much Yahweh has blessed them.

questions.q: What must they remember during the Festival of Weeks?
questions.a: They must remember that they were slaves in Egypt.

questions.q: What festival are the Israelites instructed to keep for seven days after they have gathered in the harvest from their threshing floors and from their wine presses?
questions.a: They are to keep the Festival of Shelters for seven days after they have gathered in their harvest.

questions.q: How much is every male Israelite supposed to give to Yahweh instead of coming without an offering?
questions.a: Every male Israelite is to give in proportion to how much Yahweh has blessed him with that year.

questions.q: At what the three festivals must all the males of Israel gather to worship Yahweh at the place that Yahweh chooses?
questions.a: They must gather to worship Yahweh at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks, and at the Festival of Shelters.

questions.q: Where are the Israelites to find their judges and officers?
questions.a: The judges and officers will be taken from each of their tribes to judge the people with righteous judgment.

questions.q: Why are the judges not to show partiality or take a bribe?
questions.a: If a judge takes a bribe, he will find it difficult to judge fairly but will instead want to do what the person who bribes him wants him to do.

questions.q: Why must the judges pursue righteousness and judge fairly?
questions.a: They must pursue righteousness and judge fairly, so that they may live and occupy the land that Yahweh is giving them.

questions.q: What are the Israelites not to set up for themselves?
questions.a: They are not to set up an Asherah pole or a stone pillar to worship any idol.

commentary.text: Of judges, Groves and images forbidden.

Verses 1–17 The laws for the three yearly feasts are here repeated; that of the Passover, that of the Pentecost, that of Tabernacles; and the general law concerning the people's attendance. Never should a believer forget his low estate of guilt and misery, his deliverance, and the price it cost the Redeemer; that gratitude and joy in the Lord may be mingled with sorrow for sin, and patience under the tribulations in his way to the kingdom of heaven. They must rejoice in their receivings from God, and in their returns of service and sacrifice to him; our duty must be our delight, as well as our enjoyment. If those who were under the law must rejoice before God, much more we that are under the grace of the gospel; which makes it our duty to rejoice evermore, to rejoice in the Lord always. When we rejoice in God ourselves, we should do what we can to assist others also to rejoice in him, by comforting the mourners, and supplying those who are in want. All who make God their joy, may rejoice in hope, for He is faithful that has promised.

Care is taken for the due administration of justice. All personal regards must be laid aside, so that right is done to all, and wrong to none. Care is taken to prevent following the idolatrous customs of the heathen. Nothing belies God more, or tends more to corrupt the minds of men, than representing and worshipping, by an image, that God, who is an almighty and eternal Spirit, present every where. Alas! even in gospel days, and under a better dispensation, established upon better promises, there is a tendency to set up idols, under one form or another, in the human heart.
